                                                         *vllm.models.qwen3_5*

Qwen3.5 model --- hardware-isolated entry point.

The NVIDIA and ROCm variants use the eager + breakable CUDA-graph
modelling code with explicit fused kernels. XPU uses a separate eager +
breakable XPU-graph implementation with explicit routed/shared expert
fusion for eligible MoE calls. All other platforms keep the previous
torch.compile implementation in `vllm/model_executor/models/` so their
behavior is unchanged.

Modules: ~

amd
common
nvidia
xpu

                video_grid_thw: Tensor `(n_videos, 3)` of video 3D grid
                in LLM. `None` if no videos are passed.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                   *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.amd.hyperconnection*

HyperConnection (Gated Residual) utilities for the AMD model variant.

Implements the HyperConnection residual scheme proposed in
"HyperConnections" (https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.19606). This AMD variant
delays each HC combine to the following HC mix boundary. HC glue
kernels, including fused combine+RMSNorm, live in `ops/hc.py`;
projections remain standard vLLM Linear modules.

Hidden states between layers have shape `[..., HC*HS]` with HS inner (HC
outer, HS inner --- checkpoint-native layout).

Typical usage inside a transformer decoder layer:

>python
    self.attn_hc = GatedResidual(hc_config)

    hidden_states, block_input, injection = self.attn_hc.mix(hidden_states)
    attention_output = attention(block_input)
    hidden_states, block_input, injection = self.mlp_hc.combine_and_mix(
        hidden_states, attention_output, injection
    )
<
Classes: ~

GatedResidual          Gated HyperConnection with learnable low-rank mixing
                       and injection.
HyperConnectionConfig  Configuration shared by all HyperConnection variants.

                     *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.amd.hyperconnection.GatedResidual*

GatedResidual
    Bases: `Module`

    Gated HyperConnection with learnable low-rank mixing and injection.

    `combine_and_mix()` runs the pre pipeline (grouped GemmaRMSNorm ->
    merged low-rank down+inject GEMM -> silu -> up GEMM -> sigmoid ->
    gated mean over the HC streams). When passed a pending block output
    and an injection, it fuses their residual combine with the RMSNorm.
    Final mixers use `use_combine=False` and do not produce a new
    injection.

    Weights: the norm owns the grouped GemmaRMSNorm affine; the
    projections are vLLM Linear modules (merged replicated linear for
    down+inject), so GEMM dispatch (e.g. the low-latency skinny GEMM)
    applies through the standard quant_method mechanism.

    Methods: ~

    combine_and_mix  Consume a pending combine, then prepare the next block
                     input.

    combine_and_mix(hidden_states, prev_block_output, prev_injection)
    *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.amd.hyperconnection.GatedResidual.combine_and_mix*
        Consume a pending combine, then prepare the next block input.

        `hidden_states` is the multi-stream state from before the
        pending block's mix. Its combine with `block_output` is fused
        with this module's input RMSNorm.

             *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.amd.hyperconnection.HyperConnectionConfig*

_remap_qsa_cache_scale_name(name, qsa_layer_ids)
    Map serialized main-cache scales onto the merged QSA owner.

    Regular attention keeps cache scales below its `attn` child. QSA
    owns that cache directly, so only QSA layers need the final path
    component moved to the owner's persistent `_k_scale`/`_v_scale`
    buffers.

                                               *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.amd.mtp*

Inference-only Qwen4Exp MTP (Multi-Token Predictor) model.

The MTP draft model reuses the Qwen4Exp backbone (PLE/HC/MoE) but: -
drops all multi-modal handling (text-only), - forces PLE off while
keeping the main model's HC stream count, - fuses the backbone hidden
and the new-token embedding via `residual_linear_shared` (fc_embedding +
shared fc_hidden) instead of the `Linear(2H, H)` + repeat used by other
MTP variants, - emits TWO hidden streams per step (scheme A): a single
stream [T, H] (final-mixer collapsed, fed to the LM head) and a
pre-final-mixer multi stream [T, hc_count*H] (fed to the next draft
step).

       *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.amd.ple_layer.qwen4_exp_amd_ple_ngram_embedding*

qwen4_exp_amd_ple_ngram_embedding(ngram_ids, output, layer_name)
    Run the large PLE embedding lookup outside Inductor's FX graph.

    Keeping the embedding weight in `static_forward_context` prevents
    AOT compile-time autotuning from materializing a synthetic copy of
    the weight.

*vllm.models.qwen4_exp.amd.ple_layer.qwen4_exp_amd_ple_ngram_embedding_pinned*

qwen4_exp_amd_ple_ngram_embedding_pinned(ngram_ids, output, layer_name)
    Run the pinned PLE UVA lookup outside Inductor's FX graph.

    Same rationale as the device-path escape: keeping the large
    embedding weight out of the graph prevents AOT compile-time
    autotuning from materializing a synthetic copy of the weight.

             *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.amd.ple_layer.qwen4_exp_amd_ple_ngram_ids*

qwen4_exp_amd_ple_ngram_ids(input_ids, query_start_loc, ngram_context, output,
    layer_name)
    Hash the current request layout into n-gram embedding indices.

    The launch sizes its request binary search from the request count,
    which is symbolic under Dynamo, so it runs outside Inductor's FX
    graph.

                                    *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.amd.qsa.QSAIndexer*

QSAIndexer
    Bases: `Module`

    Replicated Q/K projection plus paged, weight-free QSA selection.

    `prefix` must be the checkpoint's indexer prefix, normally
    `model.layers.N.self_attn.indexer`. Consequently the trainable names
    are `index_qk_proj`, `q_layernorm` and `k_layernorm` under that
    prefix.

    Methods: ~

    forward                    Return fixed-width request-relative token
                               indices padded with `-1`.
    normalize_compressed_keys  Normalize pooled K and apply the first token's
                               exact group position.
    project                    Project replicated Q/K and split, leaving both
                               operands unrotated.
    project_qk                 Project replicated Q/K, normalize+rotate Q, and
                               preserve raw K.

    _fused_prepare(projected_q, raw_keys, positions, raw_metadata,
        compressed_metadata, attn, qkv, slot_mapping, gate_out)
    *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.amd.qsa.QSAIndexer._fused_prepare*
        Prepare the indexer and `attn`'s main attention in one launch.

        Normalizes and rotates the index Q, compresses K and writes both
        side caches, which replaces `project_qk`'s norm/RoPE half and
        the whole of `_update_and_compress`. The same launch applies
        `attn`'s QK-norm and RoPE, copies its gate and writes its K/V
        into `attn.kv_cache`, replacing `_project_qkv_gate` and
        `do_kv_cache_update`. Both halves must stay numerically
        interchangeable with what they replace.

    forward(hidden_states, positions, out=None, *, attn, qkv=None,
        slot_mapping=None, gate_out=None)
    *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.amd.qsa.QSAIndexer.forward*
        Return fixed-width request-relative token indices padded with
        `-1`.

        With `attn.use_fused_qsa_prepare`, the same launch also writes
        `attn`'s K/V into `attn.kv_cache` at `slot_mapping` and prepares
        its Q and gate from `qkv`, returned as the second element (None
        otherwise). The gate is written into `gate_out` when given.
        `qkv`, `slot_mapping` and `gate_out` are only read in that mode.

    normalize_compressed_keys(compressed_keys, first_rope_positions)
    *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.amd.qsa.QSAIndexer.normalize_compressed_keys*
        Normalize pooled K and apply the first token's exact group
        position.

    project(hidden_states)
    *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.amd.qsa.QSAIndexer.project*
        Project replicated Q/K and split, leaving both operands
        unrotated.

    project_qk(hidden_states, positions)
    *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.amd.qsa.QSAIndexer.project_qk*
        Project replicated Q/K, normalize+rotate Q, and preserve raw K.

                            *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.amd.qsa.Qwen4ExpQSABackend*

Qwen4ExpQSABackend
    Bases: `AttentionBackend`

    Full-attention backend used by the merged QSA owner.

    With an Octave `kv_cache_dtype` the main K/V cache holds one packed
    Octave slot per (token, KV head) and sparse attention runs the
    Octave sparse decode kernel over the selected positions.

        With `attn.use_fused_qsa_prepare`, the same launch also writes
        `attn`'s K/V into `attn.kv_cache` at `slot_mapping` and prepares

        otherwise). The gate is written into `gate_out` when given.
        `qkv`, `slot_mapping` and `gate_out` are only read in that mode.

                                  *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.common.GatedResidual*

GatedResidual
    Bases: `HyperConnectionBase`

    Gated HyperConnection with learnable low-rank mixing and injection.

    `mix()` applies GemmaRMSNorm per HC stream and projects through a
    low-rank sigmoid gate to produce a single block input. `combine()`
    injects the block output back into each stream through a learned
    per-stream injection weight.

    This implementation uses only PyTorch operators. Tensor-parallel
    collectives are supplied by its caller.

    Methods: ~

    mix  Mix: RMSNorm -> low-rank gate -> gated mean.

    mix(hyper_input)
    *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.common.GatedResidual.mix*
        Mix: RMSNorm -> low-rank gate -> gated mean.

                            *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.common.HyperConnectionBase*

HyperConnectionBase
    Bases: `Module`

    Average-pooling HyperConnection (`hyperconnection_average`).

    Splits the incoming `[..., HC*HS]` tensor (HC outer, HS inner) into
    `HC` parallel streams, averages them for the block input, and
    broadcasts the block output back to every stream.

    Methods: ~

    combine  Broadcast the block output back to every stream.
    mix      Average the HC streams into a single block input.

    combine(block_output, residual)
    *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.common.HyperConnectionBase.combine*
        Broadcast the block output back to every stream.

    mix(hyper_input)
    *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.common.HyperConnectionBase.mix*
        Average the HC streams into a single block input.

                              *vllm.models.step5.amd.model.Step5SparseIndexer*

Step5SparseIndexer
    Bases: `Module`

    MQA indexer with `heads_per_group` query heads per KV group.

    Q and W are sharded like the attention KV heads, so each rank
    computes only its own groups; the shared single-head K and Z stay
    replicated.

    Methods: ~

    forward  Returns `(q [T, G, 8, P] fp8, k [T, 1, P], z [T, 1, P],

    forward(hidden_states, positions, decode=None)
    *vllm.models.step5.amd.model.Step5SparseIndexer.forward*
        Returns
        `(q [T, G, 8, P] fp8, k [T, 1, P], z [T, 1, P], w [T, G, 8])`
        for this rank's `G` local groups, heads padded to 8.

        With `decode=(summary cache, ring, slots)` it also stores each
        token's open-region row and summarizes the regions it closes.

                                             *vllm.multimodal.audio.AudioSpec*

AudioSpec  dataclass
    Specification for target audio format.

    This dataclass defines the expected audio format for a model's
    feature extractor. It is used to normalize audio data before
    processing.

    Attributes: ~
        target_channels (int | None)
            Number of output channels. None means passthrough (no
            normalization). 1 = mono, 2 = stereo, etc.

        channel_reduction (ChannelReduction)
            Method to reduce channels when input has more channels than
            target. Only used when reducing channels.

    needs_normalization property
    *vllm.multimodal.audio.AudioSpec.needs_normalization*
        Whether audio normalization is needed.

                                      *vllm.multimodal.audio.find_split_point*

find_split_point(wav, start_idx, end_idx, min_energy_window)
    Find the best point to split audio by looking for silence or low
    amplitude.

    Searches for the quietest region within a specified range by
    calculating RMS energy in sliding windows.

    Parameters: ~
        wav (ndarray)
            1D mono audio array.

        start_idx (int)
            Start index of search region (inclusive).

        end_idx (int)
            End index of search region (exclusive).

        min_energy_window (int)
            Window size in samples for energy calculation.

    Returns: ~
        int
            Index of the quietest point within the search region. This
            is the

        int
            recommended split point to minimize audio artifacts.

      Example: ~

            audio = np.random.randn(32000)

            Insert quiet region *vllm.multimodal.audio.find_split_point--insert-quiet-region*

            audio[16000:17600] = 0.01 split_idx = find_split_point( ...
            wav=audio, ... start_idx=0, ... end_idx=32000, ...
            min_energy_window=1600, ... ) 16000 <= split_idx <= 17600
            True

                                       *vllm.multimodal.audio.normalize_audio*

normalize_audio(audio, spec)
    Normalize audio to the specified format.

    This function handles channel reduction for multi-channel audio,
    supporting both numpy arrays and torch tensors.

    Parameters: ~
        audio (NDArray[floating] | Tensor)
            Input audio data. Can be: - 1D array/tensor: (time,) -
            already mono - 2D array/tensor: (channels, time) - standard
            format from torchaudio - 2D array/tensor: (time, channels) -
            format from soundfile (will be auto-detected and transposed
            if time > channels)

        spec (AudioSpec)
            AudioSpec defining the target format.

    Returns: ~
        NDArray[floating] | Tensor
            Normalized audio in the same type as input (numpy or torch).

        NDArray[floating] | Tensor
            For mono output (target_channels=1), returns 1D
            array/tensor.

    Raises: ~
        ValueError
            If audio has unsupported dimensions or channel expansion is
            requested (e.g., mono to stereo).

                             *vllm.multimodal.audio.resample_audio_torchaudio*

resample_audio_torchaudio(audio, *, orig_sr, target_sr)
    Resample audio using torchaudio's bandlimited sinc interpolation.

    Unlike the PyAV resampler, this handles any input length without
    padding and applies the kernel over the trailing axis, so 2D
    `(channels, samples)` input needs no per-channel loop.

    Parameters: ~
        audio (NDArray[floating])
            Input audio. Can be: - 1D array `(samples,)`: mono audio -
            2D array `(channels, samples)`: stereo audio

        orig_sr (float)
            Original sample rate in Hz.

        target_sr (float)
            Target sample rate in Hz.

    Returns: ~
        NDArray[floating]
            Resampled audio with the same shape as the input (1D → 1D,
            2D → 2D).

                                           *vllm.multimodal.audio.split_audio*

split_audio(audio_data, sample_rate, max_clip_duration_s, overlap_duration_s,
    min_energy_window_size)
    Split audio into chunks with intelligent split points.

    Splits long audio into smaller chunks at low-energy regions to
    minimize cutting through speech. Uses overlapping windows to find
    quiet moments for splitting.

    Parameters: ~
        audio_data (ndarray)
            1D mono audio array to split. ASR models consume mono, so
            callers must downmix before chunking.

        sample_rate (int)
            Sample rate of the audio in Hz.

        max_clip_duration_s (float)
            Maximum duration of each chunk in seconds.

        overlap_duration_s (float)
            Overlap duration in seconds between consecutive chunks. Used
            to search for optimal split points.

        min_energy_window_size (int)
            Window size in samples for finding low-energy regions.

    Returns: ~
        list[ndarray]
            List of 1D audio chunks.

    Raises: ~
        AssertionError
            If `audio_data` is not 1D.

      Example: ~

            audio = np.random.randn(1040000) # 65 seconds at 16kHz
            chunks = split_audio( ... audio_data=audio, ...
            sample_rate=16000, ... max_clip_duration_s=30.0, ...
            overlap_duration_s=1.0, ... min_energy_window_size=1600, ...
            ) len(chunks) 3

                         *vllm.multimodal.cache.LruKeyReplicatedReceiverCache*

LruKeyReplicatedReceiverCache
    Bases: `BaseMultiModalReceiverCache`

    The cache which is used on P1 when LRU caching is enabled.

    How to update each item:

    - If the caller sent tensor data, store it (replacing any cached
      item under the same key) and return that data. P0 can miss after
      independent LRU eviction and resend a different item for the same
      identity.
    - If the caller sent no data and the item is cached, return the
      cached item.
    - If the caller sent no data and the item is not cached, raise
      `MultiModalCacheMissError`.

                           *vllm.multimodal.cache.LruKeyReplicatedSenderCache*

LruKeyReplicatedSenderCache
    Bases: `BaseMultiModalProcessorCache`

    The cache which is used on P0 when LRU caching is enabled.

    How to update each item:

    - If the item is already in the cache, clear the input to avoid
      unnecessary IPC.
    - If the item is not in the cache, store the metadata of that item
      so that the eviction policy remains the same as the cache on P1,
      and return the input. By only storing the metadata, we avoid
      keeping the data itself in memory inside P0.

                              *vllm.multimodal.cache.MultiModalCacheMissError*

MultiModalCacheMissError
    Bases: `RuntimeError`

    Raised by the P1 receiver cache when items are requested with no
    data and are not cached.

    P0 (frontend) keeps a metadata-only shadow of P1 (engine) and sends
    `data=None` on a shadow hit. The two caches are updated in different
    orders across processes, so they can drift -- leaving P0 referencing
    items P1 has evicted. Raising (instead of asserting) lets the engine
    return a retryable response and have P0 drop the stale entries
    (`BaseMultiModalProcessorCache.invalidate`) so the client resends
    the data. Carries every drifted `mm_hash` in the request so P0 can
    drop them all in one pass -- one retry then recovers the whole
    request, not one item per retry.

                          *vllm.multimodal.cache.MultiModalProcessorOnlyCache*

MultiModalProcessorOnlyCache
    Bases: `BaseMultiModalProcessorCache`

    The cache which is used on P0 when IPC caching is disabled.

    How to update each item:

    - If the item is in the cache, replace the input with the cached
      item.
    - If the item is not in the cache, store that item (which includes
      tensor data and metadata) into the cache, and return the input.

                           *vllm.multimodal.cache.ShmObjectStoreReceiverCache*

ShmObjectStoreReceiverCache
    Bases: `BaseMultiModalReceiverCache`

    The cache which is used on P1 Worker Process when SHM caching is
    enabled.

    How to update each item:

    - If the item has an address, replace the input with the cached
      item.
    - If not, return the input.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                              *vllm.multimodal.gpu_ipc_memory*

Admission control for frontend GPU-side multimodal work.

When multimodal media is decoded on the GPU in the API-server (frontend)
process, the decoded buffers compete for the same device memory that the
engine reserves for weights, activations, and the KV cache. To keep the
frontend's GPU usage within a sequestered budget (see
`MultiModalConfig.mm_ipc_gpu_memory_gb`), decode paths acquire the
number of bytes they need from a process-global
`MultiModalGPUMemoryPool` before allocating on the device and release
them once the device memory is freed.

The pool is a simple byte-counting semaphore: `acquire` blocks until
enough budget is free, so concurrent requests serialize rather than
oversubscribe the GPU. It lives only in the frontend process; the engine
carves the matching amount out of its KV-cache budget so the headroom
physically exists.

Classes: ~

MultiModalGPUMemoryLease  A handle for bytes acquired from a
                          `MultiModalGPUMemoryPool`.
MultiModalGPUMemoryPool   Blocking byte-counting semaphore for frontend GPU
                          multimodal memory.

Functions: ~

get_mm_gpu_ipc_pool         Return the process-global pool, or `None` when
                            gating is disabled.
maybe_init_mm_gpu_ipc_pool  Create and install the global pool from the
                            configured GiB budget.
reserve_mm_ipc_gpu_memory   Return KV-cache memory remaining after frontend
                            multimodal reservations.
set_mm_gpu_ipc_pool         Install the process-global pool (frontend process
                            only).

                     *vllm.multimodal.gpu_ipc_memory.MultiModalGPUMemoryLease*

MultiModalGPUMemoryLease
    A handle for bytes acquired from a `MultiModalGPUMemoryPool`.

    Releasing is idempotent and the lease doubles as a context manager
    so the budget is returned even if the decode raises.

                      *vllm.multimodal.gpu_ipc_memory.MultiModalGPUMemoryPool*

MultiModalGPUMemoryPool
    Blocking byte-counting semaphore for frontend GPU multimodal memory.

    Thread-safe in both directions: `acquire` (blocking) and `release`
    are typically called from the renderer's multimodal executor
    threads.

    Methods: ~

    acquire  Reserve `nbytes`, blocking until that much budget is free.

    acquire(nbytes)
    *vllm.multimodal.gpu_ipc_memory.MultiModalGPUMemoryPool.acquire*

        capacity, since such a request could never be satisfied.

                          *vllm.multimodal.gpu_ipc_memory.get_mm_gpu_ipc_pool*

                   *vllm.multimodal.gpu_ipc_memory.maybe_init_mm_gpu_ipc_pool*

maybe_init_mm_gpu_ipc_pool(mm_ipc_gpu_memory_gb, api_process_count=1)
    Create and install the global pool from the configured GiB budget.

    Returns `None` (and leaves gating disabled) when the budget is 0.
    When multiple API-server processes share one engine, each process
    gets an equal slice of the user-provided frontend budget.

                    *vllm.multimodal.gpu_ipc_memory.reserve_mm_ipc_gpu_memory*

reserve_mm_ipc_gpu_memory(available_kv_cache_memory_bytes, mm_config,
    api_process_count=1)
    Return KV-cache memory remaining after frontend multimodal
    reservations.

    The reservation covers:

    - The total `mm_ipc_gpu_memory_gb` budget for transient
      decoded-frame buffers. This budget is divided among API processes,
      so it is not multiplied by `api_process_count`.
    - For GPU video backends, a fixed upper bound for each API process's
      retained decoder surfaces and CUDA context. The PyNvVideoCodec
      surface reservation scales with its configured `hw_decoders`
      value, and the entire decoder reservation scales with
      `api_process_count` because these resources are not shared between
      processes.

    Parameters: ~
        available_kv_cache_memory_bytes (int)
            KV-cache capacity before reserving memory for frontend
            multimodal processing.

        mm_config (MultiModalConfig | None)
            Multimodal configuration, or `None` when multimodal
            processing is disabled.

        api_process_count (int, default: 1)
            Number of frontend API processes sharing the GPU. Values
            below one are treated as one.

    Returns: ~
        int
            KV-cache capacity after subtracting the frontend
            reservation.

    Raises: ~
        ValueError
            If the reservation leaves no memory for the KV cache.

                          *vllm.multimodal.gpu_ipc_memory.set_mm_gpu_ipc_pool*

                                     *vllm.multimodal.hasher.MultiModalHasher*

MultiModalHasher
    Derives multi-modal cache keys.

    Every method here yields framed chunks: each chunk is preceded by
    its length and each container by its kind, so that the concatenation
    fed to the digest is uniquely decodable and distinct inputs cannot
    share a key.

    Methods: ~

                         container kind.

    iter_value_to_bytes(obj) classmethod
    *vllm.multimodal.hasher.MultiModalHasher.iter_value_to_bytes*

                                       *vllm.multimodal.MultiModalKwargsItems*

MultiModalKwargsItems
    Bases: `UserDict[str, Sequence[_I]]`

    A dictionary of processed multi-modal inputs by modality.

    For example, given a processor that processes images into
    `pixel_values` and `image_grid_thw`, and audios into
    `input_audio_features`, a prompt with 2 images and 1 audio will be
    processed into a `MultiModalKwargsItems` with the following
    structure:

    >python
        MultiModalKwargsItems(
            {
                "image": [
                    # For the first image
                    MultiModalKwargsItem({"pixel_values": ..., "image_grid_thw": ...}),
                    # For the second imgae
                    MultiModalKwargsItem({"pixel_values": ..., "image_grid_thw": ...}),
                ],
                "audio": [
                    # For the first audio
                    MultiModalKwargsItem({"input_audio_features": ...}),
                ],
            }
        )
<
    Unlike HF processing which returns all items in a single dictionary
    with batched keyword arguments, we split up the items because some
    of them may already be cached. Also, items from multiple requests
    may be batched together to improve throughput, using the logic
    defined by the |vllm.multimodal.inputs.BaseMultiModalField| for each
    keyword argument.

    Methods: ~

    get_data  Construct a dictionary of keyword arguments to pass to the
              model.

    get_data(*, device=None, pin_memory=False)
    *vllm.multimodal.MultiModalKwargsItems.get_data*
        Construct a dictionary of keyword arguments to pass to the
        model.

                                *vllm.multimodal.inputs.MultiModalKwargsItems*

MultiModalKwargsItems
    Bases: `UserDict[str, Sequence[_I]]`

    A dictionary of processed multi-modal inputs by modality.

    For example, given a processor that processes images into
    `pixel_values` and `image_grid_thw`, and audios into
    `input_audio_features`, a prompt with 2 images and 1 audio will be
    processed into a `MultiModalKwargsItems` with the following
    structure:

    >python
        MultiModalKwargsItems(
            {
                "image": [
                    # For the first image
                    MultiModalKwargsItem({"pixel_values": ..., "image_grid_thw": ...}),
                    # For the second imgae
                    MultiModalKwargsItem({"pixel_values": ..., "image_grid_thw": ...}),
                ],
                "audio": [
                    # For the first audio
                    MultiModalKwargsItem({"input_audio_features": ...}),
                ],
            }
        )
<
    Unlike HF processing which returns all items in a single dictionary
    with batched keyword arguments, we split up the items because some
    of them may already be cached. Also, items from multiple requests
    may be batched together to improve throughput, using the logic
    defined by the |vllm.multimodal.inputs.BaseMultiModalField| for each
    keyword argument.

    Methods: ~

    get_data  Construct a dictionary of keyword arguments to pass to the
              model.

    get_data(*, device=None, pin_memory=False)
    *vllm.multimodal.inputs.MultiModalKwargsItems.get_data*
        Construct a dictionary of keyword arguments to pass to the
        model.

                                     *vllm.multimodal.inputs.PlaceholderRange*

PlaceholderRange dataclass
    Placeholder location information for multi-modal data.

    Example: Prompt: `AAAA BBBB What is in these images?`

    Images A and B will have:

    >text
        A: PlaceholderRange(offset=0, length=4)
        B: PlaceholderRange(offset=5, length=4)
<
    Methods: ~

    extract_embeds_range         Extract the start and end indices of the
                                 embedded region in prompt.
    get_embeds_indices_in_range  Returns the starting and ending indices of
                                 the embeddings of encoder outputs

    Attributes: ~
        is_embed (Tensor | None)
            A boolean mask of shape `(length,)` indicating which positions

        length (int)
            The length of the placeholder.

        offset (int)
            The start index of the placeholder in the prompt.

    is_embed = None class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.multimodal.inputs.PlaceholderRange.is_embed*
        A boolean mask of shape `(length,)` indicating which positions
        between `offset` and `offset + length` to assign embeddings to.

    length instance-attribute
    *vllm.multimodal.inputs.PlaceholderRange.length*
        The length of the placeholder.

    offset instance-attribute
    *vllm.multimodal.inputs.PlaceholderRange.offset*
        The start index of the placeholder in the prompt.

    extract_embeds_range()
    *vllm.multimodal.inputs.PlaceholderRange.extract_embeds_range*
        Extract the start and end indices of the embedded region in
        prompt.

        For example, given `PlaceholderRange(offset=2, length=5)` and
        `is_embed = [False, True, False, True, True]`, the output is
        `[(1 + offset, 1 + offset), (3 + offset, 4 + offset)]`.

        Returns: ~
            list[tuple[int, int]]
                A tuple `(start, end)` representing the start and end

            list[tuple[int, int]]
                indices (inclusive) of the embedded region.

            list[tuple[int, int]]
                Returns full placeholder range if `is_embed` is `None`.

    get_embeds_indices_in_range(start_idx, end_idx)
    *vllm.multimodal.inputs.PlaceholderRange.get_embeds_indices_in_range*
        Returns the starting and ending indices of the embeddings of
        encoder outputs in the range of [start_idx, end_idx) in the
        placeholders.

        For example, given: PlaceholderRange(offset=2, length=5,
        is_embed=[False, True, False, True, True])

        If start_idx=3 and end_idx=5, the output is (1, 3) because we
        want to get the second and the third embeddings from the encoder
        output.

                                            *vllm.multimodal.inputs._is_dense*

_is_dense(t)
    Whether `t`'s elements fill a contiguous storage range, possibly
    permuted (e.g. a transposed matrix). Such layouts can be copied with
    pitched cudaMemcpy2D/3DAsync directly from pinned memory, whereas
    gapped layouts (e.g. strided slices) stage through a pageable temp.

                                        *vllm.multimodal.media.MediaWithBytes*

MediaWithBytes  dataclass
    Bases: `Generic[_T]`

    Wrapper that couples a media object with its original encoded bytes.

    This ensures the raw bytes and media object remain synchronized,
    preventing cache corruption from in-place modifications.

    The wrapper delegates attribute access to the underlying media
    object, making it behave transparently like the wrapped type (e.g.,
    PIL.Image).

    NOTE: Currently, this wrapper is used only for the image and video
    modalities.

    Methods: ~

    __array__    Allow np.array(obj) to return np.array(obj.media).
    __getattr__  Delegate attribute access to the underlying media object.
    __getitem__  Allow obj[i] to index obj.media (e.g. video tuples).
    __iter__     Allow unpacking obj to unpack obj.media (e.g. video tuples).

    Attributes: ~
        io_config (dict[str, Any] | None)
            Decode settings that altered the media relative to
            `original_bytes`

    io_config = None class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.multimodal.media.MediaWithBytes.io_config*
        Decode settings that altered the media relative to
        `original_bytes` (e.g. `image_mode` conversion), so they
        participate in cache hashing.

    __array__(*args, **kwargs)
    *vllm.multimodal.media.MediaWithBytes.__array__*
        Allow np.array(obj) to return np.array(obj.media).

    __getattr__(name)
    *vllm.multimodal.media.MediaWithBytes.__getattr__*
        Delegate attribute access to the underlying media object.

    __getitem__(index)
    *vllm.multimodal.media.MediaWithBytes.__getitem__*
        Allow obj[i] to index obj.media (e.g. video tuples).

    __iter__()
    *vllm.multimodal.media.MediaWithBytes.__iter__*
        Allow unpacking obj to unpack obj.media (e.g. video tuples).

                                          *vllm.multimodal.media.VideoMediaIO*

VideoMediaIO
    Bases:
    `MediaIO[MediaWithBytes[tuple[DecodedFrames, dict[str, Any]]]]`

    Configuration values can be user-provided either by
    --media-io-kwargs or by the runtime API field "media_io_kwargs".

    Use --media-io-kwargs '{"video": {"backend": "torchcodec", "device":
    "cuda"}}' to decode with NVDEC and keep frames on the GPU, which
    pairs with a device-side multi-modal processor

                                    *vllm.multimodal.parse.EmbeddingFieldRole*

EmbeddingFieldRole = Literal['values', 'metadata'] module-attribute
    What a field of a pre-computed-embedding input carries.

    `"values"` is the embedding tensor itself; `"metadata"` is a key
    that sizes the prompt's placeholder range. The distinction is what
    lets one declaration serve both an ordinary request (everything
    present) and an EC consumer (embeddings arrive through the
    connector, metadata still in the request).

    embedding_fields = {} class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.multimodal.parse.MultiModalDataParser.embedding_fields*
        Per-modality field roles for pre-computed-embedding inputs.

        Declared here rather than inside `_parse_*_data` so an EC
        producer can read it too: on a producer the request carries real
        media, so the branch that builds `DictEmbeddingItems` never
        runs, yet the producer still has to know which processed keys to
        publish. One declaration, both sides, no drift.

        A modality absent from this mapping can only be sent whole in
        the request.

    _parse_vision_chunk_data(data)
    *vllm.multimodal.parse.MultiModalDataParser._parse_vision_chunk_data*

    *vllm.multimodal.parse.MultiModalDataParser.embedding_field_sets*
        `modality`'s (required, optional) fields for this deployment.

        Resolves the static roles in `embedding_fields` against where
        the embeddings actually come from: on an EC consumer they arrive
        through the connector, so the request may omit them; anywhere
        else a request that claims to carry pre-computed embeddings has
        to actually carry them.

validate_embedding_ndim(tensor, modality, index=None)
    Validate tensor ndim for multimodal embeddings.

    embeddings should be 3D (batch, seq_len, hidden_size).

    get_mm_max_tokens_per_item(seq_len, mm_counts)
    *vllm.multimodal.processing.context.BaseProcessingInfo.get_mm_max_tokens_per_item*
        Return the maximum number of tokens per item of for each
        modality.

        When `None` (the default) is returned, vLLM will generate dummy
        inputs (images/videos) at maximum possible sizes and process
        them to determine the maximum token count per modality.

        This approach works but can be very slow for certain models
        (e.g., Qwen2.5-VL), leading to very long startup time. For
        better performance, each model can override this method to
        return pre-computed maximum token counts, avoiding the need for
        dummy input generation and processing.

          Note: ~

          The maximum number of tokens per item of each modality
          returned from this function should respect the model's maximum
          sequence length and the maximum number of items of each
          modality allowed, and agree with dummy inputs (images/videos)
          at maximum possible sizes.

    get_supported_mm_limits()
    *vllm.multimodal.processing.context.BaseProcessingInfo.get_supported_mm_limits*
        Return the maximum supported number of items for each modality.

        A value of `None` means unlimited number of items.

        Omitting a modality from the returned dictionary means that it
        is not supported at all.

    get_supported_mm_processor_kwargs()
    *vllm.multimodal.processing.context.BaseProcessingInfo.get_supported_mm_processor_kwargs*
        Return supported kwarg names for each HF processor kwargs scope.

    get_video_frame_limits()
    *vllm.multimodal.processing.context.BaseProcessingInfo.get_video_frame_limits*
        The `max_frames`/`min_frames` of the HF video processor, which
        the video loader samples to; empty for models without one.

    get_merged_mm_kwargs(kwargs, *, supported_mm_processor_kwargs=None)
    *vllm.multimodal.processing.context.InputProcessingContext.get_merged_mm_kwargs*
        Merge configured and request `mm_processor_kwargs`.

        When `supported_mm_processor_kwargs` is provided, flat keys are
        matched against the keys supported by each HuggingFace processor
        kwarg scope. Matching flat keys are routed to every scope that
        supports them and removed from the shared flat namespace; keys
        not supported by any scope remain flat.

        Without `supported_mm_processor_kwargs`, flat keys already
        represented in at least one existing mapping-valued scope are
        removed from the shared flat namespace; all other flat keys are
        left unchanged because there is no information to determine
        which scopes should receive them.

             *vllm.multimodal.processing.context._resolve_mm_processor_kwargs*

_resolve_mm_processor_kwargs(kwargs, supported_mm_processor_kwargs=None)
    Resolve flat processor kwargs into HuggingFace processor kwarg
    scopes.

    With `supported_mm_processor_kwargs`, each scope lists the flat keys
    it supports. Matching flat keys are routed to every scope that
    supports them, existing scoped values take precedence, and keys not
    supported by any scope remain flat.

    Without `supported_mm_processor_kwargs`, flat keys already
    represented in at least one existing mapping-valued scope are
    removed from the shared flat namespace; all other flat keys are left
    unchanged because there is no information to determine which scopes
    should receive them.

    _apply_prompt_updates_via_text(token_ids, mm_prompt_updates, *,
        encode_segments_separately=False)
    *vllm.multimodal.processing.BaseMultiModalProcessor._apply_prompt_updates_via_text*
        Apply multi-modal prompt updates in text space, then encode the
        result.

        A non-special-token target may be tokenized differently inside
        the prompt because the tokens may go across the boundaries of
        the target (e.g. when searching for "foo" in "food", if "food"
        itself makes up a token, then the token ID of "foo" will not
        appear at all). Since it is inefficient to search for all
        possible tokenizations of the target in the prompt, we instead
        perform text-based updates on the decoded token IDs, then encode
        them back.

    _cached_apply_hf_processor(inputs, timing_ctx)
    *vllm.multimodal.processing.BaseMultiModalProcessor._cached_apply_hf_processor*
        Apply the HF processor on the full prompt text, caching the
        results and reusing cached results.

    abstractmethod
    *vllm.multimodal.processing.BaseMultiModalProcessor._get_prompt_updates*
        Given the original multi-modal items for this modality and
        HF-processed data, output the updates to perform.

        The information returned by this method is used to update token
        inputs which bypass the HF processor. It is also used to update
        the output of HF processor if the HF process does not apply
        prompt updates to text inputs.

        Moreover, this information is critical to determine the token
        positions in order to construct
        |vllm.multimodal.inputs.PlaceholderRange| for each multi-modal
        item.

    apply(inputs, timing_ctx)
    *vllm.multimodal.processing.BaseMultiModalProcessor.apply*
        Process multi-modal inputs to be used in vLLM.

        The main steps are:

        1. Perform MM-specific post-processing to the token inputs.
        2. Apply HF Processor on multi-modal data together with optional
           dummy text, outputting processed multi-modal data tensors.
        3. Find and update sequences in the token IDs with placeholder
           tokens. The number of placeholder tokens equals the feature
           size of the multi-modal data outputted by the multi-modal
           encoder.
        4. Extract information about the placeholder tokens from the
           processed token IDs.

    get_mm_max_tokens_per_item(seq_len, mm_counts)
    *vllm.multimodal.processing.BaseProcessingInfo.get_mm_max_tokens_per_item*
        Return the maximum number of tokens per item of for each
        modality.

        When `None` (the default) is returned, vLLM will generate dummy
        inputs (images/videos) at maximum possible sizes and process
        them to determine the maximum token count per modality.

        This approach works but can be very slow for certain models
        (e.g., Qwen2.5-VL), leading to very long startup time. For
        better performance, each model can override this method to
        return pre-computed maximum token counts, avoiding the need for
        dummy input generation and processing.

          Note: ~

          The maximum number of tokens per item of each modality
          returned from this function should respect the model's maximum
          sequence length and the maximum number of items of each
          modality allowed, and agree with dummy inputs (images/videos)
          at maximum possible sizes.

    get_supported_mm_limits()
    *vllm.multimodal.processing.BaseProcessingInfo.get_supported_mm_limits*
        Return the maximum supported number of items for each modality.

        A value of `None` means unlimited number of items.

        Omitting a modality from the returned dictionary means that it
        is not supported at all.

    get_merged_mm_kwargs(kwargs, *, supported_mm_processor_kwargs=None)
    *vllm.multimodal.processing.InputProcessingContext.get_merged_mm_kwargs*
        Merge configured and request `mm_processor_kwargs`.

        When `supported_mm_processor_kwargs` is provided, flat keys are
        matched against the keys supported by each HuggingFace processor
        kwarg scope. Matching flat keys are routed to every scope that
        supports them and removed from the shared flat namespace; keys
        not supported by any scope remain flat.

        Without `supported_mm_processor_kwargs`, flat keys already
        represented in at least one existing mapping-valued scope are
        removed from the shared flat namespace; all other flat keys are
        left unchanged because there is no information to determine
        which scopes should receive them.

                                  *vllm.multimodal.processing.PromptInsertion*

PromptInsertion dataclass
    Bases: `PromptUpdate`

    Defines how to insert placeholder tokens into a prompt.

    Example: For each image, insert a number of `<image>` feature
    placeholders equal to the feature size of the vision encoder after
    the `<s>` token:

    >python
        PromptInsertion(
            modality="image",
            target=[bos_token_id],
            insertion=[image_token_id] * image_feature_size,
        )
<
    Insert these tokens at the start of the prompt:

    >python
        PromptInsertion(
            modality="image",
            target=PromptIndexTargets.start(),
            insertion=[image_token_id] * image_feature_size,
        )
<
    Insert these tokens after a prefix `Images:`:

    >python
        PromptInsertion(
            modality="image",
            target=PromptIndexTargets.prefix(images_prefix_token_ids),
            insertion=[image_token_id] * image_feature_size,
        )
<
    Insert these tokens at the end of the prompt:

    >python
        PromptInsertion(
            modality="image",
            target=PromptIndexTargets.end(),
            insertion=[image_token_id] * image_feature_size,
        )
<
    Attributes: ~
        insertion (PromptUpdateContent)
            Given the index of the processed item within

    insertion = field(repr=False) class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.multimodal.processing.PromptInsertion.insertion*
        Given the index of the processed item within
        |vllm.multimodal.processing.PromptUpdate.modality|, output the
        token sequence to insert right after
        |vllm.multimodal.processing.PromptUpdate.target|.

        For convenience, you can directly pass in the token sequence
        instead of a function if it does not depend on the input.

                                *vllm.multimodal.processing.PromptReplacement*

PromptReplacement dataclass
    Bases: `PromptUpdate`

    Defines how to replace portions of an input prompt with placeholder
    tokens.

    Example: For each image, replace one `<image>` input placeholder in
    the prompt with a number of `<image>` feature placeholders equal to
    the feature size of the vision encoder:

    >python
        PromptReplacement(
            modality="image",
            target=[image_token_id],
            replacement=[image_token_id] * image_feature_size,
        )
<
    As above, but further pad the feature placeholders with
    `<image_bos>` and `<image_eos>`, which are not supposed to be passed
    to the vision encoder:

    >python
        PromptReplacement(
            modality="image",
            target=[image_token_id],
            replacement=PromptUpdateDetails(
                full=(
                    [image_bos_id] + [image_token_id] * image_feature_size + [image_eos_id]
                ),
                is_embed=lambda full: torch.tensor(full) == image_token_id,
            ),
        )
<
    Attributes: ~
        replacement (PromptUpdateContent)
            Given the index of the processed item within

    replacement = field(repr=False) class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.multimodal.processing.PromptReplacement.replacement*
        Given the index of the processed item within
        |vllm.multimodal.processing.PromptUpdate.modality|, output the
        token sequence to replace
        |vllm.multimodal.processing.PromptUpdate.target|.

        For convenience, you can directly pass in the token sequence
        instead of a function if it does not depend on the input.

                *vllm.multimodal.processing.processor.BaseMultiModalProcessor*

BaseMultiModalProcessor
    Bases: `ABC`, `Generic[_I]`

    Abstract base class to process multi-modal inputs to be used in
    vLLM.

    Not to be confused with `transformers.ProcessorMixin`.

    Methods: ~

    apply                Process multi-modal inputs to be used in vLLM.
    get_dummy_inputs     Build the input which, after processing, results in
    get_dummy_mm_inputs  Create dummy data for profiling the memory usage of a
                         model.

    _apply_hf_processor_main(mm_items, hf_kwargs)
    *vllm.multimodal.processing.processor.BaseMultiModalProcessor._apply_hf_processor_main*
        Apply the HF processor on the multi-modal data.

    _apply_prompt_updates(token_ids, mm_prompt_updates)
    *vllm.multimodal.processing.processor.BaseMultiModalProcessor._apply_prompt_updates*
        Apply multi-modal prompt updates to token IDs.

    _apply_prompt_updates_via_text(token_ids, mm_prompt_updates, *,
        encode_segments_separately=False)
    *vllm.multimodal.processing.processor.BaseMultiModalProcessor._apply_prompt_updates_via_text*
        Apply multi-modal prompt updates in text space, then encode the
        result.

        A non-special-token target may be tokenized differently inside
        the prompt because the tokens may go across the boundaries of
        the target (e.g. when searching for "foo" in "food", if "food"
        itself makes up a token, then the token ID of "foo" will not
        appear at all). Since it is inefficient to search for all
        possible tokenizations of the target in the prompt, we instead
        perform text-based updates on the decoded token IDs, then encode
        them back.

    _cached_apply_hf_processor(inputs, timing_ctx)
    *vllm.multimodal.processing.processor.BaseMultiModalProcessor._cached_apply_hf_processor*
        Apply the HF processor on the full prompt text, caching the
        results and reusing cached results.

    _get_prompt_updates(mm_items, hf_processor_mm_kwargs, out_mm_kwargs)
    abstractmethod
    *vllm.multimodal.processing.processor.BaseMultiModalProcessor._get_prompt_updates*
        Given the original multi-modal items for this modality and
        HF-processed data, output the updates to perform.

        The information returned by this method is used to update token
        inputs which bypass the HF processor. It is also used to update
        the output of HF processor if the HF process does not apply
        prompt updates to text inputs.

        Moreover, this information is critical to determine the token
        positions in order to construct
        |vllm.multimodal.inputs.PlaceholderRange| for each multi-modal
        item.

    _iter_text_matches(update, prompt_text, tokenizer, *, start_idx=0)

    _postprocess_hf_mm_data(mm_data, hf_processor_mm_kwargs, processed_data)
    *vllm.multimodal.processing.processor.BaseMultiModalProcessor._postprocess_hf_mm_data*
        Post-process the combined processor and passthrough data.

        By default, the output is returned as-is. If you need to modify
        the output of the HF processor before it is converted into
        multi-modal keyword arguments, you should override this method.

    _postprocess_prompt(prompt)
    *vllm.multimodal.processing.processor.BaseMultiModalProcessor._postprocess_prompt*
        Post-process the prompt token IDs before locating or applying
        multi-modal prompt updates.

        By default, the prompt is returned as-is. If the HF processor
        (or chat template) applies additional transformations to the
        prompt that are not reflected in its multi-modal outputs, you
        should override this method to replicate them.

    _recompute_cached_prompt_update(cached_update, new_item_idx)
    *vllm.multimodal.processing.processor.BaseMultiModalProcessor._recompute_cached_prompt_update*
        Override this if other attributes of `ResolvedPromptUpdate` also
        need to be recomputed after retrieving from the cache.

    apply(inputs, timing_ctx)
    *vllm.multimodal.processing.processor.BaseMultiModalProcessor.apply*
        Process multi-modal inputs to be used in vLLM.

        The main steps are:

        1. Perform MM-specific post-processing to the token inputs.
        2. Apply HF Processor on multi-modal data together with optional
           dummy text, outputting processed multi-modal data tensors.
        3. Find and update sequences in the token IDs with placeholder
           tokens. The number of placeholder tokens equals the feature
           size of the multi-modal data outputted by the multi-modal
           encoder.
        4. Extract information about the placeholder tokens from the
           processed token IDs.

    get_dummy_inputs(seq_len, mm_counts, mm_options)

                        *vllm.multimodal.processing.processor.PromptInsertion*

PromptInsertion dataclass
    Bases: `PromptUpdate`

    Defines how to insert placeholder tokens into a prompt.

    Example: For each image, insert a number of `<image>` feature
    placeholders equal to the feature size of the vision encoder after
    the `<s>` token:

    >python
        PromptInsertion(
            modality="image",
            target=[bos_token_id],
            insertion=[image_token_id] * image_feature_size,
        )
<
    Insert these tokens at the start of the prompt:

    >python
        PromptInsertion(
            modality="image",
            target=PromptIndexTargets.start(),
            insertion=[image_token_id] * image_feature_size,
        )
<
    Insert these tokens after a prefix `Images:`:

    >python
        PromptInsertion(
            modality="image",
            target=PromptIndexTargets.prefix(images_prefix_token_ids),
            insertion=[image_token_id] * image_feature_size,
        )
<
    Insert these tokens at the end of the prompt:

    >python
        PromptInsertion(
            modality="image",
            target=PromptIndexTargets.end(),
            insertion=[image_token_id] * image_feature_size,
        )
<
    Attributes: ~
        insertion (PromptUpdateContent)
            Given the index of the processed item within

    insertion = field(repr=False) class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.multimodal.processing.processor.PromptInsertion.insertion*
        Given the index of the processed item within
        |vllm.multimodal.processing.PromptUpdate.modality|, output the
        token sequence to insert right after
        |vllm.multimodal.processing.PromptUpdate.target|.

        For convenience, you can directly pass in the token sequence
        instead of a function if it does not depend on the input.

                      *vllm.multimodal.processing.processor.PromptReplacement*

PromptReplacement dataclass
    Bases: `PromptUpdate`

    Defines how to replace portions of an input prompt with placeholder
    tokens.

    Example: For each image, replace one `<image>` input placeholder in
    the prompt with a number of `<image>` feature placeholders equal to
    the feature size of the vision encoder:

    >python
        PromptReplacement(
            modality="image",
            target=[image_token_id],
            replacement=[image_token_id] * image_feature_size,
        )
<
    As above, but further pad the feature placeholders with
    `<image_bos>` and `<image_eos>`, which are not supposed to be passed
    to the vision encoder:

    >python
        PromptReplacement(
            modality="image",
            target=[image_token_id],
            replacement=PromptUpdateDetails(
                full=(
                    [image_bos_id] + [image_token_id] * image_feature_size + [image_eos_id]
                ),
                is_embed=lambda full: torch.tensor(full) == image_token_id,
            ),
        )
<
    Attributes: ~
        replacement (PromptUpdateContent)
            Given the index of the processed item within

    replacement = field(repr=False) class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.multimodal.processing.processor.PromptReplacement.replacement*
        Given the index of the processed item within
        |vllm.multimodal.processing.PromptUpdate.modality|, output the
        token sequence to replace
        |vllm.multimodal.processing.PromptUpdate.target|.

        For convenience, you can directly pass in the token sequence
        instead of a function if it does not depend on the input.

                           *vllm.multimodal.processing.processor.PromptUpdate*

PromptUpdate dataclass
    Bases: `ABC`

    Defines how to update a prompt with placeholder tokens.

      Note: ~

      The target and content are token sequences. When converting text
      to token sequences, remember to encode it with
      `add_special_tokens=False` to match how the prompt itself is
      tokenized. Otherwise, the updated prompt may contain duplicated
      special tokens or fail to match the target.

                             *vllm.multimodal.utils.group_and_batch_mm_kwargs*

group_and_batch_mm_kwargs(mm_kwargs, *, device=None, pin_memory=False)
    Group consecutive items (possibly from different requests) into
    batches.

    Items must be split across groups if any of the following occurs, as
    the batch would otherwise be invalid: - They have different fields
    (e.g. mixed image and embedding inputs). - They have different
    values in `MultiModalSharedField`.

    To simplify the implementation of `embed_multimodal`, we add another

                             *vllm.multimodal.utils.set_mm_embedding_modality*

set_mm_embedding_modality(embed, modality, placement=None)
    Attach modality metadata to a gathered multimodal embedding tensor.

    Used by interleaved Omni merge paths that need to group embeddings
    by modality without threading a parallel modalities list through
    `embed_input_ids`.

    `placement` is `(start, end, is_embed)`: the embedding fills the
    batch positions `[start, end)` selected by the CPU mask `is_embed`
    (all of them if `None`). It lets models build per-modality position
    masks without reading `input_ids` on the host.

                                 *vllm.multimodal.utils.strip_covered_mm_data*

strip_covered_mm_data(mm_features, num_computed_tokens, uses_mrope=False)
    Drop the tensor data of mm items whose placeholder span is fully
    inside a prefix-cache-covered region: no encoder run can be
    scheduled for them, so the workers never consume the payload fields.
    M-RoPE models keep CPU-side metadata fields used to compute
    positions. SHM address items are also kept so workers can balance
    the sender's reference count. The scheduler-side `Request` keeps the
    full features.

                                  *vllm.multimodal.video.ClefOmniVideoBackend*

ClefOmniVideoBackend
    Bases: `VideoBackend`

    Clef-Omni's reference sampling: the first frame at or after each
    `1/fps` boundary (frame i sits at `i / original_fps` seconds, so the
    k-th boundary is crossed by frame `ceil(k * original_fps / fps)`),
    capped at 768 frames and padded to an even count by repeating the
    last frame.

                                   *vllm.multimodal.video.DynamicVideoBackend*

DynamicVideoBackend
    Bases: `VideoBackend`

    Duration-aware dynamic-sampling video backend.

    Samples at `fps` up to `max_duration` seconds, falling back to
    uniform sampling across the full duration when the video is longer
    than `max_duration`. Codec is selectable the same way as
    `VideoBackend`.

                                    *vllm.multimodal.video.GLM46VVideoBackend*

GLM46VVideoBackend
    Bases: `VideoBackend`

    GLM-4.6V dynamic FPS video backend.

    Faithfully replicates the frame sampling logic from transformers'
    `Glm46VVideoProcessor.sample_frames`:

    - Dynamic FPS thresholds based on effective video duration:
      `{≤30s: 3fps, ≤300s: 1fps, >300s: 0.5fps}`
    - `temporal_patch_size` multiplier (default 2) applied to extract
      count
    - Duration capped at 2400s, frame count capped at 640
    - Even frame count enforced (append last frame if odd)

                                  *vllm.multimodal.video.Glm5NextVideoBackend*

Glm5NextVideoBackend
    Bases: `VideoBackend`

    GLM-5.3-Flash fps-interval video backend.

    Selects frames with the same sampler the processor falls back to, so
    only the sampled frames are materialized. `fps_interval` semantics
    (default 2.0) with a temporal-patch-scaled greedy walk, frame count
    capped at 2048, temporal pairs kept even. Request overrides: `fps`
    -> fps interval, `max_frames` -> frame cap, `temporal_patch_size`
    (default 2).

    _sample_frame_indices(total_frames, fps, duration, *, target_fps=None,
        max_frame_count=None, temporal_patch_size=2) classmethod
    *vllm.multimodal.video.Glm5NextVideoBackend._sample_frame_indices*
        GLM video frame sampling (training-reference parity).

        `target_fps` is the `fps_interval` request knob. The greedy walk
        advances at `1 / (temporal_patch_size * target_fps)` seconds, so
        on frame-dense sources it collects more candidates than
        `extract_t` and the `> extract_t` fixup re-spreads the picks
        uniformly with `np.linspace` -- that fallback is the intended
        reference behavior, not an accident. Short clips (fewer frames
        than `extract_t`) are spread at evenly spaced timestamps
        (`floor` sampling; the linspace variant samples frames unevenly
        and cost 4 points on video grounding evals). Request overrides:
        `target_fps` -> fps interval, `max_frame_count` -> frame cap.

                            *vllm.multimodal.video.PyNvVideoCodecVideoBackend*

PyNvVideoCodecVideoBackend
    Bases: `VideoBackend`

    Hardware-accelerated video backend using PyNvVideoCodec.

    The backend first opens the stream only to read metadata and compute
    the sampled frame indices. It then acquires the raw decoded RGB byte
    count from the process-local multimodal GPU memory pool before
    decoding the selected frames into VRAM. Decoded frames are copied
    into pinned host memory before the lease is released, so downstream
    preprocessing continues to receive a CPU `np.ndarray` in NHWC RGB
    format.

                                   *vllm.multimodal.video.Qwen2VLVideoBackend*

Qwen2VLVideoBackend
    Bases: `VideoBackend`

    Qwen2-VL / Qwen2.5-VL fps-based video backend.

    Ports transformers' `Qwen2VLVideoProcessor.sample_frames` (fps
    mode), shared by Qwen2-VL and Qwen2.5-VL (the latter has no video
    processor of its own): sample `total / original_fps * fps` frames,
    clamp to `[min_frames, max_frames]` (4 and 768), floor to a multiple
    of `temporal_patch_size` (2), and take indices with the exact
    `torch.arange(0, total, total / n)` call so they match HF
    byte-for-byte.

    `num_frames` is ignored (fps-driven, like the Qwen3-VL loader). The
    float32 step can emit an out-of-range tail index (e.g. 451 for a
    451-frame clip); it is clamped to the last valid frame.

                                          *vllm.multimodal.video.VideoBackend*

VideoBackend
    Bases: `VideoLoader`

    Uniform-sampling video backend.

    Samples `num_frames` uniformly across the video (or one frame every
    `1/fps` seconds, whichever produces fewer frames). The decoding
    codec is selected via the `backend` kwarg (`"opencv"`,
    `"torchcodec"`, `"pynvvideocodec"`, or `"deepstream"`), which can be
    passed through `--media-io-kwargs`. Defaults to `"opencv"`.

    Methods: ~

    load_bytes  Load sampled frames from raw video bytes.

    load_bytes(data, num_frames=-1, fps=-1, max_duration=300,
        frame_recovery=False, *, backend='opencv', **kwargs) classmethod
    *vllm.multimodal.video.VideoBackend.load_bytes*
        Load sampled frames from raw video bytes.

        Parameters: ~
            data (bytes)
                Raw video bytes.

            num_frames (int, default: -1)
                Target number of frames to sample (`-1` for all).

            fps (int, default: -1)
                Target FPS for sampling (`-1` for original).

            max_duration (int, default: 300)
                Maximum duration in seconds --- only used by the dynamic
                subclass; ignored here.

            frame_recovery (bool, default: False)
                Enable forward-scan recovery for failed frames. Only
                honored by the OpenCV codec.

            backend (VideoDecoderBackend, default: 'opencv')
                Decoding codec --- `"opencv"`, `"torchcodec"`,
                `"pynvvideocodec"` or `"deepstream"`.

            kwargs (Any, default: {})
                Codec-specific options, validated against and forwarded
                to `backend`:

                - `num_ffmpeg_threads` (TorchCodec): number of FFmpeg
                  decoding threads; `0` (default) relies on the FFmpeg
                  default value which is `min(cpu_count + 1, 16)`.
                  OpenCV will always use `min(cpu_count, 16)`.
                - `seek_mode` (TorchCodec): `"exact"` (default)
                  guarantees frame-accurate sampling by scanning the
                  file on creation, while `"approximate"` skips that
                  scan for faster decoder creation at the cost of
                  relying on the file's metadata. See
                  https://meta-pytorch.org/torchcodec/stable/generated_examples/decoding/approximate_mode.html
                  for details.
                - `device` (TorchCodec): `"cpu"` (default) decodes on
                  the host and returns a `np.ndarray`; `"cuda"` decodes
                  with NVDEC and returns the frames as a CUDA
                  `torch.Tensor`, which a device-side HF video processor
                  can consume without a host round-trip.
                - `hw_decoders` (PyNvVideoCodec): maximum number of
                  concurrent decoder slots. Defaults to 2 and must be a
                  positive integer.
                - `max_width` / `max_height` (PyNvVideoCodec): optional
                  maximum input dimensions configured for each decoder.
                  Both must be positive integers and set together.
                  Values are clamped to each codec's hardware limits. By
                  default, decoder dimensions also cover the input's
                  opposite orientation when that fits the reserved
                  memory and hardware limits.
                - `pool_size` / `timeout_sec` (DeepStream): decoder pool
                  size and pool acquisition timeout in seconds.

        Returns: ~
            DecodedFrames
                Tuple of `(frames, metadata_dict)`, where `frames` is a

            dict[str, Any]
                CPU `np.ndarray` unless TorchCodec decodes on
                `device="cuda"`.

                          *vllm.multimodal.video_decoders.SampledFramesCharge*

SampledFramesCharge
    Charges the decoded size of sampled video frames to a request
    budget.

    `VideoMediaIO` installs one with `charging_sampled_frames` while a
    loader runs. Decoders call `charge_sampled_frames` once they know
    the frame size and the sampled indices, so an oversized sample is
    rejected before any frame is decoded.

                                                *vllm.parser.DelegatingParser*

DelegatingParser
    Bases: `Parser`

    A Parser implementation that delegates to separate ReasoningParser
    and ToolParser instances.

    This is the recommended base class for creating model-specific
    parsers that combine existing reasoning and tool parser
    implementations. Subclasses should set `self._reasoning_parser` and
    `self._tool_parser` in their `__init__` method.

    If either parser is None, the corresponding methods will return
    default values (no reasoning extraction, no tool calls).

    Methods: ~

    _align_heterogeneous_kv_block_size(vllm_config, backend_cls)
    classmethod
    *vllm.platforms.Platform._align_heterogeneous_kv_block_size*
        Align block size when several KV dtypes share one block pool.

        A quantized primary (e.g. nvfp4) shares the block pool with one
        or more higher-precision "padded specs" (skip layers today; the
        first/last-N sibling in the future). A padded spec's per-token
        page is larger than the primary's and not an integer multiple of
        it, so the trivial `unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size` cannot
        reconcile them. We do it here instead, before the specs are
        built:

        1. Bump the primary `block_size` (kernel-aligned) until the
           primary page is large enough to cover the largest padded-spec
           page.
        2. Record that shared page in each padded spec's
           `*_page_size_padded` hint, so it pads up to the shared page.

        `unify` then sees equal pages and stays trivial.

        To add a padded-spec type: append its per-token page to
        `padded_pages` and set its `*_page_size_padded` hint below.

    _align_hybrid_block_size(vllm_config, backend_cls) classmethod
    *vllm.platforms.Platform._align_hybrid_block_size*
        For hybrid attention/mamba models, ensure that the attention
        page size is >= the mamba page size, and pad the mamba page size
        to match.

    _check_aligned_block_size(vllm_config, backend_classes, pre_block_size)
    classmethod
    *vllm.platforms.Platform._check_aligned_block_size*
        Fail now, not at worker setup, if alignment left a rejected
        size.

        Alignment rounds by the first backend's kernel block only, so it
        can land on a size a sibling backend rejects.

    _find_non_ssm_backends(vllm_config) classmethod
    *vllm.platforms.Platform._find_non_ssm_backends*
        Distinct non-SSM attention backends, in layer order.

    _preferred_block_size_for_backends(backend_classes, default_block_size,
        vllm_config) classmethod
    *vllm.platforms.Platform._preferred_block_size_for_backends*
        Block size every backend accepts.

        One backend keeps its preferred size. When every backend accepts
        the default, several backends keep that preference only when
        they all ask for the same size and all accept it. Differing
        preferences keep the default. If any backend rejects the
        default, the LCM search is unchanged.

        `supports_block_size` may be overridden to accept exact sizes
        only (CPU_MLA takes 16 and no multiple of it), so candidates are
        the LCMs of one supported size per backend, each checked against
        every backend.

        Raises: ~
            ValueError
                If the backends share no supported block size.

    apply_config_platform_defaults(vllm_config) classmethod
    *vllm.platforms.Platform.apply_config_platform_defaults*
        Apply the platform-specific default values to the config.

        This function is called during the initialization of global
        VllmConfig, after parsing cli arguments. It can modify the
        defaults of the config according to the platform. For example,
        it can enable custom_ops based on the enabled features.

        The config is passed by reference, so it can be modified in
        place.

    *vllm.platforms.Platform.check_runner_kv_caches_multi_layer*
        Check whether the platform's ModelRunner can handle multiple
        attention layers that share the same layer index (e.g. cross
        attention and self attention in the same decoder block of an
        encoder-decoder model such as BART).

        Platforms that have verified that their `runner_kv_caches` is
        not impacted by this case should override this to a no-op.
        Otherwise the default implementation raises
        `NotImplementedError`.

    get_kv_cache_config_builder_cls(vllm_config) classmethod
    *vllm.platforms.Platform.get_kv_cache_config_builder_cls*
        Resolve the fully-qualified class path of the platform's KV
        cache config builder.

          Note: ~

          Experimental, like the `KVCacheConfigBuilder` interface it
          selects.

        The builder supplies grouping (`get_kv_cache_groups`) and tensor
        placement (`get_kv_cache_config_from_groups`). Vendors may
        override this to return a platform-specific builder. The default
        builder honors a model implementing `SupportsKVCacheGrouping`; a
        builder that overrides `get_kv_cache_groups` owns grouping and
        bypasses that model hook unless it calls `super()`.

        Returns: ~
            str
                Fully-qualified class path of a `KVCacheConfigBuilder`
                subclass.

        override this to return it directly. The default implementation
        selects the best backend from a device-capability-based priority
        list.

        Returns: ~

        Raises: ~

                configuration.

    is_fp8_fnuz() classmethod
    *vllm.platforms.Platform.is_fp8_fnuz*
        Returns whether the preferred FP8 type is FNUZ on the current
        platform.

        There are two representations of FP8, OCP FP8 and FNUZ FP8. The
        OCP specification can be found at https://tinyurl.com/b7jvwpft.
        The FNUZ specification can be found at
        https://tinyurl.com/5n6hwwu5.

        AMD's MI300 and MI325 have native hardware support for FNUZ. All
        other hardware has converged on the OCP FP8 standard.

    is_integrated_gpu(device_id=0) classmethod
    *vllm.platforms.Platform.is_integrated_gpu*
        Returns whether the GPU is an integrated (UMA) device that
        shares system memory with the CPU. device_id None means the
        current device.

        On UMA systems (e.g. NVIDIA GH200, DGX Spark, Jetson Orin),
        cudaMemGetInfo may underreport free memory because it does not
        account for reclaimable OS memory (page cache, buffers).

    *vllm.platforms.Platform.logical_device_id_to_visible_device_id*
        Map a vLLM-local logical device ID to the current process's
        visible accelerator ordinal.

        vLLM internals use logical local IDs. Physical IDs are used only
        at platform/topology boundaries. This helper performs the final

    _align_heterogeneous_kv_block_size(vllm_config, backend_cls)
    classmethod
    *vllm.platforms.interface.Platform._align_heterogeneous_kv_block_size*
        Align block size when several KV dtypes share one block pool.

        A quantized primary (e.g. nvfp4) shares the block pool with one
        or more higher-precision "padded specs" (skip layers today; the
        first/last-N sibling in the future). A padded spec's per-token
        page is larger than the primary's and not an integer multiple of
        it, so the trivial `unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size` cannot
        reconcile them. We do it here instead, before the specs are
        built:

        1. Bump the primary `block_size` (kernel-aligned) until the
           primary page is large enough to cover the largest padded-spec
           page.
        2. Record that shared page in each padded spec's
           `*_page_size_padded` hint, so it pads up to the shared page.

        `unify` then sees equal pages and stays trivial.

        To add a padded-spec type: append its per-token page to
        `padded_pages` and set its `*_page_size_padded` hint below.

    _align_hybrid_block_size(vllm_config, backend_cls) classmethod
    *vllm.platforms.interface.Platform._align_hybrid_block_size*
        For hybrid attention/mamba models, ensure that the attention
        page size is >= the mamba page size, and pad the mamba page size
        to match.

    _check_aligned_block_size(vllm_config, backend_classes, pre_block_size)
    classmethod
    *vllm.platforms.interface.Platform._check_aligned_block_size*
        Fail now, not at worker setup, if alignment left a rejected
        size.

        Alignment rounds by the first backend's kernel block only, so it
        can land on a size a sibling backend rejects.

    _find_non_ssm_backends(vllm_config) classmethod

    _preferred_block_size_for_backends(backend_classes, default_block_size,
        vllm_config) classmethod
    *vllm.platforms.interface.Platform._preferred_block_size_for_backends*
        Block size every backend accepts.

        One backend keeps its preferred size. When every backend accepts
        the default, several backends keep that preference only when
        they all ask for the same size and all accept it. Differing
        preferences keep the default. If any backend rejects the
        default, the LCM search is unchanged.

        `supports_block_size` may be overridden to accept exact sizes
        only (CPU_MLA takes 16 and no multiple of it), so candidates are
        the LCMs of one supported size per backend, each checked against
        every backend.

        Raises: ~
            ValueError
                If the backends share no supported block size.

    apply_config_platform_defaults(vllm_config) classmethod

    get_kv_cache_config_builder_cls(vllm_config) classmethod
    *vllm.platforms.interface.Platform.get_kv_cache_config_builder_cls*
        Resolve the fully-qualified class path of the platform's KV
        cache config builder.

          Note: ~

          Experimental, like the `KVCacheConfigBuilder` interface it
          selects.

        The builder supplies grouping (`get_kv_cache_groups`) and tensor
        placement (`get_kv_cache_config_from_groups`). Vendors may
        override this to return a platform-specific builder. The default
        builder honors a model implementing `SupportsKVCacheGrouping`; a

        bypasses that model hook unless it calls `super()`.

                subclass.

    is_fp8_fnuz() classmethod
    *vllm.platforms.interface.Platform.is_fp8_fnuz*
        Returns whether the preferred FP8 type is FNUZ on the current
        platform.

        There are two representations of FP8, OCP FP8 and FNUZ FP8. The
        OCP specification can be found at https://tinyurl.com/b7jvwpft.
        The FNUZ specification can be found at
        https://tinyurl.com/5n6hwwu5.

        AMD's MI300 and MI325 have native hardware support for FNUZ. All
        other hardware has converged on the OCP FP8 standard.

    is_integrated_gpu(device_id=0) classmethod
    *vllm.platforms.interface.Platform.is_integrated_gpu*
        Returns whether the GPU is an integrated (UMA) device that
        shares system memory with the CPU. device_id None means the
        current device.

        On UMA systems (e.g. NVIDIA GH200, DGX Spark, Jetson Orin),
        cudaMemGetInfo may underreport free memory because it does not
        account for reclaimable OS memory (page cache, buffers).

                      *vllm.platforms.interface.set_assigned_physical_gpu_ids*

set_assigned_physical_gpu_ids(ids)
    Set the physical GPU IDs assigned to this worker process. Called
    during worker init so that device_id_to_physical_device_id() can map
    local_rank to the correct physical device without relying on
    CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES.

    Idempotent: a second call with the same value is a no-op. Raises
    RuntimeError if called again with a different value.

    This is expected to run during single-threaded worker
    initialization.
