                                              *vllm.v1.metrics.reader.Counter*

Counter  dataclass
    Bases: `Metric`

    A monotonically increasing integer counter.

                                                *vllm.v1.metrics.reader.Gauge*

Gauge  dataclass
    Bases: `Metric`

    A numerical value that can go up or down.

                                            *vllm.v1.metrics.reader.Histogram*

Histogram  dataclass
    Bases: `Metric`

    Observations recorded in configurable buckets.

    Buckets are represented by a dictionary. The key is the upper limit
    of the bucket, and the value is the observed count in that bucket. A
    '+Inf' key always exists.

    The count property is the total count across all buckets, identical
    to the count of the '+Inf' bucket.

    The sum property is the total sum of all observed values.

                                               *vllm.v1.metrics.reader.Metric*

Metric  dataclass
    A base class for prometheus metrics.

    Each metric may be associated with key=value labels, and in some
    cases a single vLLM instance may have multiple metrics with the same
    name but different sets of labels.

                                               *vllm.v1.metrics.reader.Vector*

Vector  dataclass
    Bases: `Metric`

    An ordered array of integer counters.

    This type - which doesn't exist in Prometheus - models one very
    specific metric, vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_per_pos.

                                 *vllm.v1.metrics.reader.get_metrics_snapshot*

get_metrics_snapshot()
    An API for accessing in-memory Prometheus metrics.

      Example: ~

            for metric in llm.get_metrics(): ... if isinstance(metric,
            Counter): ... print(f"{metric} = {metric.value}") ... elif
            isinstance(metric, Gauge): ... print(f"{metric} =
            {metric.value}") ... elif isinstance(metric, Histogram): ...
            print(f"{metric}") ... print(f" sum = {metric.sum}") ...
            print(f" count = {metric.count}") ... for bucket_le, value
            in metrics.buckets.items(): ... print(f" {bucket_le} =
            {value}")

                              *vllm.v1.metrics.stats.RequestSpecDecodeMetrics*

RequestSpecDecodeMetrics dataclass
    Per-output-sequence speculative-decoding statistics accumulator.

    Accumulates, over one sequence's verify steps, a histogram of
    accepted draft-token counts (`j`, draft-only) and the total number
    of proposed draft tokens. When `detailed` is requested it also
    records the ordered per-step accepted/proposed sequences (`summary`
    omits them). Tracked per engine `Request` (one per sampled sequence,
    so `n > 1` yields one per child), surfaced via `EngineCoreOutput`
    and the response `metrics.speculative_decoding` for single-sequence
    requests (see `to_dict`).

      Fields: ~

      num_spec_tokens: Configured `num_speculative_tokens` (the max
      `k`); also the histogram's upper bound. histogram: Dense counts
      indexed by accepted draft tokens `j` (length
      `num_spec_tokens + 1`). num_draft_tokens: Total proposed draft
      tokens, including grammar-invalid ones. per_step_accepted: Ordered
      accepted-draft count per verify step (`detailed` only; empty
      otherwise). per_step_drafted: Ordered proposed-draft count per
      verify step (`detailed` only; empty otherwise).
      num_verified_tokens: Total draft tokens the target model ran a
      forward pass on. per_step_verified: Ordered verified-draft count
      per verify step (`detailed` only; empty otherwise).

    Methods: ~

    to_dict  Payload matching `SpeculativeDecodingMetrics` for the response.

    to_dict()
    *vllm.v1.metrics.stats.RequestSpecDecodeMetrics.to_dict*
        Payload matching `SpeculativeDecodingMetrics` for the response.

        `acceptance_histogram` is a dense list indexed by accepted draft
        count `j` (length `num_spec_tokens + 1`).
        `mean_acceptance_length` includes the bonus token (`j + 1`);
        `draft_acceptance_rate` is draft-only, full precision. Per-step
        arrays are included only when populated (`detailed` level).

                                         *vllm.v1.serial_utils.MsgpackDecoder*

MsgpackDecoder
    Decoder with custom torch tensor and numpy array serialization.

    Note that unlike vanilla `msgspec` Decoders, this interface is
    generally not thread-safe when encoding tensors / numpy arrays.

    `oob_tensor_provider` must be used when an OOBTensorConsumer is used
    on the encoder side.

                                         *vllm.v1.serial_utils.MsgpackEncoder*

MsgpackEncoder
    Encoder with custom torch tensor and numpy array serialization.

    Note that unlike vanilla `msgspec` Encoders, this interface is
    generally not thread-safe when encoding tensors / numpy arrays.

    By default, arrays below 256B are serialized inline Larger will get
    sent via dedicated messages. Note that this is a per-tensor limit.

    When a `oob_tensor_consumer` is provided, tensors (CUDA and CPU)
    will be offered to it for out-of-band handling.

StructuredOutputManager

    _fill_bitmasks(batch)
    *vllm.v1.structured_output.StructuredOutputManager._fill_bitmasks*
        Fill one bitmask row per entry.

        A row the grammar does not constrain allows every token except
        `masked_ids`, the implicit reasoning ends masked while
        reasoning.

    _get_constraint_bounds(request, spec_tokens, spec_tokens_committed=False)
    *vllm.v1.structured_output.StructuredOutputManager._get_constraint_bounds*
        Return the index into `spec_tokens` where tokens should start
        being constrained by the grammar. Assumes `spec_tokens` are
        stripped of -1 padding tokens. Returns `len(spec_tokens) + 1` if
        no token should be constrained after accepting all
        `spec_tokens`. This is `constraint_start`; `grammar_start` is
        one less if reasoning ends implicitly on a content token (e.g. a
        tool-call start).

        `spec_tokens_committed` is True if spec_tokens is already in
        `request.all_token_ids`.

    _masked_reasoning_ends(request)
    *vllm.v1.structured_output.StructuredOutputManager._masked_reasoning_ends*
        Implicit reasoning-end tokens the grammar rejects as first
        content.

        Such a token (e.g. a tool-call start) ends reasoning and is also
        the first content token, so sampling one where the grammar
        cannot start with it would make the output invalid. These stay
        masked while the request reasons. The grammar does not advance
        before reasoning ends, so the set is fixed per request.

    accept_tokens(request, new_token_ids)
    *vllm.v1.structured_output.StructuredOutputManager.accept_tokens*
        Advance grammar with accepted tokens. Returns False on
        rejection.

    trim_spec_tokens(request, spec_tokens)
    *vllm.v1.structured_output.StructuredOutputManager.trim_spec_tokens*
        Trim structured-output padding and grammar-invalid suffixes.

                                  *vllm.v1.token_buffer.rfind_token_sequences*

rfind_token_sequences(token_ids, markers, start=0, stop=None)
    Return `(index, k)` for the newest occurrence in
    `token_ids[start:stop]` of any of the multi-token `markers`, `k`
    being its position in `markers` (the first listed wins at the same
    index), or `(-1, -1)`.

    Candidates are found with rfind_tokens on the markers' first tokens,
    so a TokenBuffer is searched with numpy and only candidate positions
    are read.

                                           *vllm.v1.token_buffer.rfind_tokens*

rfind_tokens(token_ids, targets, start=0, stop=None)
    Return the index of the last token in `token_ids[start:stop]` that
    is one of `targets` (`None` entries, for absent tokens, are
    ignored), or -1.

    An int32 buffer (a TokenBuffer) is searched with numpy, in chunks
    growing back from `stop` so a recent match is found quickly, without
    creating a Python int per token. Other sequences are scanned
    backwards in Python.

                                            *vllm.v1.token_buffer.token_slice*

token_slice(tokens, start, stop)
    `tokens[start:stop]`; for a TokenBuffer an int32 array, so that no
    Python ints are made until it is read.

                   *vllm.v1.worker.cp_utils.should_skip_dcp_context_attention*

should_skip_dcp_context_attention(context_kv_lens_cpu)
    Whether DCP context attention can be skipped for this batch.

    Must be computed from rank-invariant inputs only (the global context
    lengths, NOT this rank's local share from get_dcp_local_seq_lens):
    the non-skip path in _forward_with_dcp issues DCP collectives (query
    all-gather + LSE combine), so every DCP rank must take the same
    branch. A rank can hold zero local context tokens while other ranks
    still hold context for the same batch.

    1. Decides if each DP rank is going to microbatch. Either all ranks
       run with microbatching or none of them do.

       across ranks), all ranks will be padded out so that they run with
       the same number of tokens.

        Uses get_load_balance_assignment() to balance load by input
        size, then select_encoder_cudagraph_items() to extract each
        rank's inputs.

        Returns: ~

                Inputs for this rank.

            image_rank_assignment (list[int])
                Flattened assignment order across all ranks.

            images_per_rank (list[int])
                Number of items per rank.

            max_output_tokens_per_rank (int)
                Max output tokens across all ranks (for padding during
                all_gather).

    _find_smallest_fitting_budget_given_tokens(total_tokens, budgets=None)
    *vllm.v1.worker.encoder_cudagraph.EncoderCudaGraphManager._find_smallest_fitting_budget_given_tokens*
        Find smallest budget >= total_tokens, or None if none fits.

    _generate_budgets(min_budget, max_budget, cap=None) staticmethod
    *vllm.v1.worker.encoder_cudagraph.EncoderCudaGraphManager._generate_budgets*
        Generate token budgets from min_budget up to max_budget or cap.

        Quarter-octave steps up to 1024 tokens, steps of 128 up to 2560,
        then 1/8-octave steps (rounded up to 128), so a replay pads at
        most ~25% below 1024, ~12% up to 2560 and ~9% above. Capture
        buffers are shared across budgets (see `_capture_budget_graph`),
        so extra graphs cost no buffer memory. Batches above the largest
        budget run eagerly.

    _get_graph_set(path='default')
    *vllm.v1.worker.encoder_cudagraph.EncoderCudaGraphManager._get_graph_set*
        Return the captured graphs for one encoder path.

    _get_item_specs(mm_kwargs)
    *vllm.v1.worker.encoder_cudagraph.EncoderCudaGraphManager._get_item_specs*
        Get item specs from the model.

    _get_per_item_out_tokens(mm_kwargs)
    *vllm.v1.worker.encoder_cudagraph.EncoderCudaGraphManager._get_per_item_out_tokens*
        Get per-item output token counts as plain ints.

    _item_multiple_budgets(item_tokens, max_budget) staticmethod
    *vllm.v1.worker.encoder_cudagraph.EncoderCudaGraphManager._item_multiple_budgets*
        Budgets for a path whose items all have item_tokens tokens.

        Every item count up to 16, then 1/8-octave steps, so batches of
        up to 16 items fit their budget exactly.

    _path_fitting_budget(path, tokens)
    *vllm.v1.worker.encoder_cudagraph.EncoderCudaGraphManager._path_fitting_budget*
        Smallest captured budget on a path; 0 when idle, None if
        oversized.

    _replay_exceeds_capture(input_buffers, replay_values)
    staticmethod
    *vllm.v1.worker.encoder_cudagraph.EncoderCudaGraphManager._replay_exceeds_capture*
        Return True when any replay tensor does not fit its capture
        buffer.

        Capture buffers have a fixed leading dimension. Copying a longer
        replay tensor raises in the padded copy path; callers must fall
        back to eager execution instead.

    _select_items(mm_kwargs, indices)
    *vllm.v1.worker.encoder_cudagraph.EncoderCudaGraphManager._select_items*
        Select the mm kwargs for `indices` from the model.

        Returns the sliced mm_kwargs together with the resolved

        without capture axes).

    _share_prefix_compatible(probe, shared) staticmethod
    *vllm.v1.worker.encoder_cudagraph.EncoderCudaGraphManager._share_prefix_compatible*
        View prefix-compatible probe buffers into the shared buffers.

        For each probe buffer that is a row-prefix of its shared
        counterpart (same trailing dims and dtype, no more rows), copy
        the probe contents into the shared buffer and return the prefix
        view instead. Anything else, including 0-dim buffers (which hold
        per-budget values and save no memory when shared), keeps its own
        per-budget allocation.

    supports_batch(modality, mm_kwargs)
    *vllm.v1.worker.encoder_cudagraph.EncoderCudaGraphManager.supports_batch*
        Check if a batch can run through the captured encoder graphs.

        Precomputed embeddings (`<modality>_embeds`) do not run the
        encoder, so the caller must send them to `embed_multimodal`
        instead. A batch never mixes them with pixel inputs:
        `group_and_batch_mm_kwargs` only batches items that have the
        same keys.

EncoderCudaGraphConfig dataclass
    Configuration for encoder CUDA graph management.

    Provided by the model at init time via

            Output hidden dim of the vision encoder.

        paths (dict[str, EncoderCudaGraphPathConfig])
            Independently captured encoder paths keyed by their forward name.

    buffer_keys instance-attribute
    *vllm.v1.worker.encoder_cudagraph_defs.EncoderCudaGraphConfig.buffer_keys*
        Keys for the tensor buffers recorded into the CUDA graph. Before
        replay the manager copies new data into these buffers, padding
        them as described in `padding_logics`.

    capture_axes = () class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.v1.worker.encoder_cudagraph_defs.EncoderCudaGraphConfig.capture_axes*
        Extra capture axes beyond the token budget; empty to disable.

        Each entry is the ordered key set of one axis. When non-empty,
        one graph is captured per token budget per combination of axis
        keys (cartesian product), so the total number of captured graphs
        is `num_budgets * prod(len(axis) for axis in capture_axes)`.

    max_frames_per_video = 1 class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.v1.worker.encoder_cudagraph_defs.EncoderCudaGraphConfig.max_frames_per_video*
        Maximum number of frames per video. Only relevant when "video"
        is in `modalities`. Image-only models can use the default of 1.

    modalities instance-attribute
    *vllm.v1.worker.encoder_cudagraph_defs.EncoderCudaGraphConfig.modalities*
        Supported modalities (e.g. ["image"]).

    out_hidden_size instance-attribute
    *vllm.v1.worker.encoder_cudagraph_defs.EncoderCudaGraphConfig.out_hidden_size*
        Output hidden dim of the vision encoder. Used for DP gather
        buffer allocation.

    padding_logics = field(default_factory=dict) class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.v1.worker.encoder_cudagraph_defs.EncoderCudaGraphConfig.padding_logics*
        Optional per-buffer replay padding/copy logic. If absent for a
        key, the manager slice-copies the replay buffer into the capture
        buffer and pads the tail with the last value for cumulative keys
        (`cu_seqlens`, `cu_window_seqlens`) or with zeros otherwise. A
        padding logic must write the whole capture buffer: budgets share
        buffers, so rows it leaves untouched may hold another budget's
        data.

    paths = field(default_factory=lambda: {'default':
        EncoderCudaGraphPathConfig()}) class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.v1.worker.encoder_cudagraph_defs.EncoderCudaGraphConfig.paths*
        Independently captured encoder paths keyed by their forward
        name.
